**Eugène Paul Louis Schueller** (20 March 1881 – 23 August 1957) was a French pharmacist and entrepreneur who was the founder of L'Oréal, the world's leading company in cosmetics and beauty.




## Founding of L'Oréal

[edit]

As a young French chemist of Alsatian paternal origin, Schueller graduated in 1904 from the Institut de Chimie Appliquée de Paris (now Chimie ParisTech). Schueller developed in 1907 an innovative hair-color formula, which he called **Oréale**. He formulated and manufactured his own products, and sold them to Parisian hairdressers.
In 1909, he registered his company, the *Société Française de Teintures Inoffensives pour Cheveux*, the future L'Oréal. The guiding principles of the company that would become L'Oréal were put into place from the start: research and innovation in the interest of beauty.[*citation needed*]



## Support for fascism

[edit]

During the early twentieth century, Schueller provided financial support and held meetings for La Cagoule at L'Oréal headquarters. La Cagoule was a violent French fascist-leaning, antisemitic and anti-communist group whose leader formed a political party Mouvement Social Révolutionnaire (MSR, Social Revolutionary Movement) which in Occupied France supported the Vichy collaboration with the conquerors from Nazi Germany.[1]


L'Oréal hired several members of the group as executives after World War II, such as Jacques Corrèze, who served as CEO of the US operation. This involvement was extensively researched by Michael Bar-Zohar in his book, *Bitter Scent*.[2]



## Family

[edit]

Schueller's daughter, Liliane Bettencourt, was the widow of André Bettencourt with whom she had one daughter, Françoise Bettencourt Meyers, chairwoman of L'Oréal's board of directors and according to Bloomberg Billionaires Index the richest woman in the world and the 12th richest person in the world, with a net worth of USD 94.9 Billion as of January 2022. Françoise Meyers is married to Jean-Pierre Meyers, whose rabbi grandfather was murdered in Auschwitz, a Nazi concentration camp.[3] In 2017, Liliane Bettencourt was the wealthiest woman in the world, with holdings estimated at US$39.5 billion.[4]



## Legacy

[edit]

The head office of L'Oréal in Clichy, Hauts-de-Seine is named *Centre Eugène Schueller*.[5]

**Avon Products, Inc.** or simply known as **Avon,** is an American[9]-British multinational cosmetics, skin care, perfume and personal care company, based in London. It sells directly to the public. Avon had annual sales of $9.1 billion worldwide in 2020.[4]


It is the fourteenth-largest beauty company[10] and, with 6.4 million representatives, is the second largest multi-level marketing enterprise in the world (after Amway).[11] The company's CEO is Angela Cretu who was appointed to the position in January 2020.[12]


In May 2019, the Brazilian multinational company Natura & Co announced its intent to acquire Avon; the deal closed in January 2020. Following the merger, existing Natura shareholders held 73% of the combined company, Natura Holding S.A., with former Avon shareholders owning 27%.[13] At merger completion, Avon became a privately held company, common stock was removed from the NYSE trading.[14]

## Major Cosmetic Brand Founding Dates

**Maybelline**: Founded in 1914 (though some sources say 1915) by pharmacist Thomas Lyle Williams in Chicago. Williams was inspired when he saw his sister Mabel applying a mixture of Vaseline and coal dust to her eyelashes to make them appear darker and fuller.

**Avon** (originally California Perfume Company): Founded in 1886 by David H. McConnell in New York City. McConnell initially sold books door-to-door but switched to selling perfumes in September 1886, starting his business in a small office at 126 Chambers Street in Manhattan.

**L'Oréal**: Founded in 1909 by Eugène Schueller in France. Schueller started by developing his own hair dye formula which he called "Aureole."

**Estée Lauder**: The company was co-founded in 1946 by Estée Lauder and her husband Joseph Lauder. Estée Lauder (1908-2004) was a pioneering American businesswoman who built her cosmetics empire after initially selling creams developed by her uncle.

## Timeline Summary
- **1886**: Avon (as California Perfume Company)
- **1909**: L'Oréal 
- **1914/1915**: Maybelline
- **1946**: Estée Lauder Companies

These founding dates show how the cosmetics industry evolved over nearly a century, from the early days of door-to-door perfume sales to the modern global beauty conglomerates we know today.
